title: Valve trombone and playing bass tuba
summary: Howard talks about playing valve trombone and the E-flat tuba, which he says are the same as the trumpet apart from the mouthpiece.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: They both made slide, I guess, all the time. Do you remember any of these vowel trombones when you were a kid? Did somebody play vowels?

Well, I never known a guy that played, but I have seen it because I have played on a vowel trombone, because it's the same thing like the trumpet, you see? And it's like the E flat bass tuba. I play, when I was waking at the farm with Morgan, under Morgan, Andrew Morgan, I used to bring the trumpet and the bass, the straight up bass tuba in place. I play, because it's the same thing. And all the difference is the mouthpiece. I mean, another way you pronounce the notes different, but things the same thing. When I play, it's a play. But I was, you know, when you're young like that, I play it, pep, energy. I think we better move those boys over there. Live! Live! Come to the bass.
I don't think the birds were too loud for that, but we can hear better enough. See, we were talking about the band of the bass and the other bands.

Yeah. Well, yeah, well, I used to play the bass and the vowel trombone, they had some, I don't know, I just remember his name, back in the middle 20s or something like that. But at vowel trombone, the only difference was the mouthpiece. You see? Yeah, that's right. They all, they all, they all, they come out the same way, like the trumpet. See? And then, in other words, you don't find many bass tuba players in New Orleans, fool with no double beat. No, it's not.
